# conda-explicit

Explicit spec files ("@EXPLICIT" lists of package URLs) written 2026-11-12 by three real
tools in throwaway containers. None of the files were edited afterwards.

- Image (all files): `docker.io/condaforge/miniforge3:latest`, digest
  `sha256:0a788afa8b54165d855d08552ce6d86e1e2553be2a9a18d542c69cfb02a6deaa`
  (conda 26.9.4, mamba 2.9.0).
- `conda-linux-64.lock`: conda-lock 4.1.0 (same venv and solver as the `conda-lock` fixture), from
  `environment.yml`, which is a copy of `conda-lock/environment.yml`:

      podman run --rm -v <scratch>:/work -w /work/explicit -e CONDA_PKGS_DIRS=/work/pkgs \
        docker.io/condaforge/miniforge3:latest \
        /work/cl-venv/bin/conda-lock lock -f environment.yml -p linux-64 --kind explicit

- `spec-file.txt`, `spec-file-sha256.txt`, `spec-file-nohash.txt` (conda 26.9.4) and
  `explicit-mamba.txt` (mamba 2.9.0; micromamba itself was not used) all come from one
  real environment with no input file. In this fixture the last three are saved, byte for byte,
  under the name conda's documentation gives an explicit spec file, one directory per variant:
  `sha256/spec-file.txt`, `nohash/spec-file.txt` and `mamba/spec-file.txt`:

      podman run --rm -v <scratch>:/work -w /work/real -e CONDA_PKGS_DIRS=/work/pkgs \
        docker.io/condaforge/miniforge3:latest bash -c '
          conda create -q -n x -y --override-channels -c conda-forge zlib xz
          conda list -n x --explicit --md5    > spec-file.txt
          conda list -n x --explicit --sha256 > spec-file-sha256.txt
          conda list -n x --explicit          > spec-file-nohash.txt
          mamba env export -n x --explicit    > explicit-mamba.txt'

  The environment has 10 packages, all linux-64 `.conda` from conda-forge: _openmp_mutex 4.5,
  libgcc 16.2.0, libgomp 16.2.0, liblzma 5.8.3, liblzma-devel 5.8.3, libzlib 1.3.2, xz 5.8.3,
  xz-gpl-tools 5.8.3, xz-tools 5.8.3 and zlib 1.3.2.

Notable features:
- `conda-linux-64.lock` (conda-lock `--kind explicit`):
  - Header lines `# Generated by conda-lock.`, `# platform: linux-64` and
    `# input_hash: d04775598fc0...`, then `@EXPLICIT`. There are no blank lines.
  - `input_hash` is conda-lock's per-platform content hash: SHA-256 of the serialized lock
    specification, not an artifact digest. It differs from `content_hash.linux-64` in the
    conda-lock fixture because that spec also had the dev and docs files.
  - 31 lines `<url>#<md5>`. The fragment is always the 32-hex MD5 of the package archive at
    `<url>`. conda-lock writes no sha256 here, even though its unified lock has one. The lines
    are in dependency order: every dependency comes before its dependent. They are the same
    URLs and MD5s as the linux-64 `main` entries of the unified lock. noarch packages are under
    `.../conda-forge/noarch/`.
  - pip packages follow as comment lines:
    `# pip six @ https://files.pythonhosted.org/.../six-1.16.0-py2.py3-none-any.whl#sha256=8abb2f1d...`
    (`#sha256=` holds the SHA-256 of the wheel) and
    `# pip tomli @ git+https://github.com/hukkin/tomli.git@36ef51d6a5a55e0eca077b58695390d041061bd4`
    (no hash; the commit is in the URL). conda-lock printed a warning that only
    `conda-lock install` and `micromamba install` install these and other tools may silently
    ignore them.
- `spec-file.txt` (`conda list --explicit --md5`): 4 comment lines (`# This file may be used to
  create an environment using:`, `# $ conda create --name <env> --file <this file>`,
  `# platform: linux-64`, `# created-by: conda 26.9.4`), `@EXPLICIT`, then 10 lines `<url>#<32-hex md5>`.
- `spec-file-sha256.txt` (`--sha256`): same header and order, but each line is `<url>#<64-hex sha256>`.
  There is **no `sha256:` prefix**, so only the length tells MD5 (32) from SHA-256 (64).
  conda's reader (`conda/misc.py` `_get_url_pattern`) accepts `#<md5>`, `#<sha256>` and
  `#sha256:<sha256>`, but this conda never writes the prefixed form. Passing `--md5 --sha256`
  together fails with `ArgumentError: Only one of --md5 and --sha256 can be specified at the same time`.
- `spec-file-nohash.txt` (`--explicit` alone): same header, bare URLs with no fragment.
- `explicit-mamba.txt` (`mamba env export --explicit`, which includes MD5 by default): only 3
  comment lines (no `# created-by:`), `@EXPLICIT`, then the same 10 `<url>#<md5>` lines in a
  different order. (`mamba list --explicit --sha256` was also tried. It prints
  `List of packages in environment: "/opt/conda/envs/x"` and no `@EXPLICIT`, so it is not a
  spec file and was not kept.)
- Digests: every digest in these files was checked by downloading the artifact. For the 10
  environment packages, the MD5 in `spec-file.txt`/`explicit-mamba.txt` and the SHA-256 in
  `spec-file-sha256.txt` equal md5sum/sha256sum of the file. The 31 MD5s in
  `conda-linux-64.lock` match as well.
- conda's writer (`print_explicit` in `conda/cli/main_list.py`) emits `# no URL for: <fn>` for a
  record without a URL. That line type does not occur in these files.
